basis.saw: bar chart of model accuracy on PubHealthBench Full and Reviewed sets

narrative.text: Figure 1 (left): PubHealthBench Full and Reviewed model accuracy across 24 LLMs. Proprietary models (GPT-4.5, GPT-4.1, o1) exceed 90% accuracy, outperforming human search baselines (88%), while open-weight models range from 45% to 85%.

basis.saw: bar chart of model accuracy on PubHealthBench FreeForm responses

narrative.text: Figure 1 (right): PubHealthBench-FreeForm model accuracy with 95% Wilson confidence intervals. Performance drops dramatically compared to MCQA, with top model o1 scoring 74% and all other models scoring below 72% (clinical guidance dropping to 57-71%).

basis.saw: sample card displaying PubHealthBench MCQA question with answer options and ground truth

narrative.text: Figure 2: Example PubHealthBench MCQA benchmark questions. Cards showing question text, four candidate answer options, ground truth guidance citation, and distractor rationale derived from UK government guidance documents.

basis.saw: flowchart of automated MCQA generation pipeline from government guidance documents

narrative.text: Figure 3: Overview of MCQA generation pipeline. Flowchart showing extraction of text from 687 UK guidance documents, filtering for chunks with actionable recommendations via Llama-3.3-70B, question and distractor generation, and automated validation.

basis.saw: stacked bar charts of benchmark question distribution by guidance topic and audience

narrative.text: Figure 4: PubHealthBench questions by guidance topic area (VPDs, immunisation, TB, AMR, environmental) and target audience (clinical guidance, public guidance, professional guidance).

basis.saw: process diagram of benchmark review and human annotation steps

narrative.text: Figure 5: Overview of benchmark review steps. Process diagram showing automated consistency filtering followed by human SME verification of question clarity, clinical validity, and reference alignment.

basis.saw: diverging bar charts of model performance deviations by topic and audience

narrative.text: Figure 6: Average deviation from overall model performance on PubHealthBench-Full by guidance topic (left) and guidance audience (right). Highlights relative difficulty of clinical guidance compared to general public health messaging.

basis.saw: confusion matrix comparing LLM-detected vs human-verified MCQA errors

narrative.text: Figure 7: Confusion matrix for LLM MCQA error detection, quantifying false positive and false negative rates during automated quality control.

basis.saw: line chart showing model accuracy plotted against document last revision date

narrative.text: Figure 8: PubHealthBench-Full MCQA accuracy by source guidance document last revision date (pre-2023 vs 2024 updates). Evaluates temporal degradation and training cutoff effects when guidance is updated after model release.

basis.saw: pie charts and bar charts of document types and human quality ratings

narrative.text: Figure 9: (left) PubHealthBench-Full samples by source text document type; (right) human quality annotations categorizing generated questions into 'Good' (82%), 'Acceptable' (15%), and 'Poor' (3%).

basis.saw: scatter and correlation plot comparing FreeForm scores across four LLM judge models

narrative.text: Figure 10: Comparison of PubHealthBench-FreeForm performance using different LLM judges (GPT-4o-Mini, Llama-3.3-70B, MedGemma-27B, Phi-4-14B). Inter-rater reliability demonstrates strong agreement with Fleiss's kappa of 0.64.

basis.saw: horizontal stacked bar chart of error categories in incorrect free form responses

narrative.text: Figure 11: Comparison of PubHealthBench-FreeForm error types classified using Llama-3.3-70B: (1) extraneous non-contradictory information, (2) omission of required points/criteria, and (3) contradiction or misstatement of official guidance.

basis.saw: breakdown chart of error distributions across model families

narrative.text: Figure 11b: Detailed breakdown of contradiction vs omission error proportions across model tiers (reasoning models vs instruction-tuned models).

basis.saw: formatted table and prompt template for LLM as a judge binary classification

narrative.text: Figure/Table 10: Judge prompt specification. Demonstrates system instructions, source guidance context injection, ground truth answer anchoring, and chain-of-thought evaluation schema for free-form responses.

basis.saw: callout comparison box showing o1 erroneous recommendation vs official guidance

narrative.text: Figure 12: Example of o1 potentially problematic response on intervention timing. Compares o1's premature clinical intervention recommendation against official UK guidance requiring specific symptom thresholds.

basis.saw: callout comparison box showing o1 delayed intervention recommendation vs official guidance

narrative.text: Figure 13: Example of o1 delayed intervention recommendation. Illustrates failure mode where model recommends waiting, contradicting urgent statutory notification guidance.

basis.saw: callout comparison box showing o1 omitted contraindication vs official guidance

narrative.text: Figure 14: Example of o1 omitted contraindication. Compares model advice recommending a vaccine without stating the crucial pregnancy/immunosuppression contraindication present in the source text.

basis.saw: callout comparison box showing o1 extraneous non-recommended intervention

narrative.text: Figure 15: Example of o1 extraneous intervention advice. Illustrates model suggesting unapproved prophylactic treatments not recognized by official UK public health guidance.

basis.saw: supplementary comparison panel of free-form evaluation edge cases

narrative.text: Figure 16: Supplementary case comparison of model deviations across infection control and post-exposure prophylaxis guidance.
